messages:
devin: Quick sync — after last week's runtime roll we saw a 20-35% drop in tokens/sec for a subset of long-sequence workloads. I'm putting together a dashboard that ties kernel selection, batch formation, and KV cache hit rate to root-cause this. Thoughts on must-have panels?

anya: +1. we need kernel fallback events on the same chart as tokens/sec. when the fused kernel falls back to slow path tokens/sec collapses.

sara: Also surface queue depth and batch utilization percentiles (p50/p95). I noticed spikes in queue depth right before the regressions.

mike: adding: token_budget_util (how much of configured token budget used per second) and batch_headroom_pct (how full batches are vs target). If headroom drops we get fragmented batches.

devin: Agreed. Proposed metric set:
- kernel_fallback_rate{model,host} (rate of kernel switches to unfused)
- tokens_per_sec{model,host}
- batch_utilization{pool} (avg tokens_in_batch / target_tokens)
- queue_depth{pool} (p50,p95)
- kv_cache_hitrate{model} (per-model prefix/KV hits)
- token_budget_consumption{route} (tokens/sec vs budget)

ranjit: Can we get a single panel that correlates kernel_fallback_rate and kv_cache_hitrate? I suspect fallback occurs when kv miss causes longer sequences (more cache misses => recompute context => different kernel path).

anya: Good call. We should also tag events where kernel selection decision flips due to sequence length threshold. Add an event stream: runtime-bot:kernel_decision_change.

runtime-bot: Deploy event stream enabled for kernel_decision_change at 2751230000.

mike: For visuals:
- Top-left: timeseries tokens_per_sec (stacked by model) with overlayed kernel_fallback_rate as bars.
- Top-right: queue_depth heatmap (pool x host) with annotations for rollout windows.
- Mid: KV cache heatmap (model x time) showing hitrate and absolute KV size.
- Bottom-left: scatter batch_utilization vs tokens_per_sec (each point = 1m window).
- Bottom-right: recent profiles link (per-minute sample) that show kernel call stacks.

devin: We need concrete alert thresholds:
- tokens_per_sec drop > 25% sustained for 3m for top-10 models => paged to eng-runtime.
- kernel_fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 5m => warn on slack channel.
- kv_cache_hitrate drop > 15% relative baseline for 10m => alert to SRE.

anya: Sampling: keep full-profile samples for 10% of requests for 2h, aggregate stacks to identify heavy kernels. For telemetry, sample QoS tags and token lengths.

sara: PromQL snippets for dashboards:
- tokens/sec: sum by (model) (rate(tokens_generated_total[1m]))
- kernel fallback rate: sum by (model) (increase(kernel_fallbacks_total[5m])) / sum by (model) (increase(kernel_decisions_total[5m]))
- kv hitrate: sum by(model) (increase(kv_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(model) (increase(kv_lookups_total[5m]))
- batch utilization: avg_over_time(batch_tokens_in_batch[5m]) / target_tokens

mike: Also add a derived metric: effective_tokens_per_sec = tokens_per_sec * (1 - kernel_fallback_rate) to show ideal vs actual.

devin: On perf regressions: profiling samples show fused attention kernel time jumps when sequence length crosses 1024 -> kernel chooses a slower code path. Put a histogram of seq_len and kernel path choice.

ranjit: Can we instrument the kernel chooser to emit a tag with reason: e.g., "seq_len_threshold", "quantization_mismatch", "workspace_alloc_fail". That will massively speed debugging.

anya: +1. add fields to kernel_decision events: reason, chosen_kernel, fallback_reason (if any), seq_len, model, host. Keep those as labels for search.

sara: Action items:
- devin: wire up dashboard panels and alerts (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- mike: add derived metrics and sampling config in telemetry repo (PR).
- ranjit: add richer kernel_decision events to runtime (small change, low risk).
- anya: make a playbook for oncall with steps to correlate kernel_fallback -> kv_hitrate -> queue_depth.

devin: I'll attach the initial profile snippet here for context:

```
# flame sample (fused_attn slow path)
fused_attention_kernel  0.48
tensor_copy             0.12
kv_cache_lookup         0.10
unfused_attention       0.08
other                   0.22
```

mike: That matches the token/sec drop. kv_cache_lookup up from 6% -> 18% during spikes. Means more misses or repeated lookups.

ranjit: I can try a fast patch to avoid kernel fallback for seq_len in [1025..1280] by forcing the fused kernels with a guard, but we need to understand memory/workspace implications. Will start a branch.

anya: Remember to annotate the dashboard with upcoming branch test windows so we can correlate. Also include canary vs prod split.

devin: Thanks everyone. I created the dashboard skeleton and shared in #eng-runtime-dashboards. Will iterate on panels tomorrow.

runtime-bot: Dashboard created: /dashboards/2751239999-batchflow-kernel-kv (view-only link).
